authorization: etymologise remaining Indo-Aryan surveys. do not rebuild. work autonomously and do what you can, you have 8 hours, i will review once your time is done.

proposals.evidence: Full ma explicitly explains the replacement of old aham by the oblique/instrumental pronoun (Prakrit maē, Apabhramsha maï̃), listing Assamese maï, Bengali mui, Oriya mu/mũ and Punjabi/Lahnda maĩ/mɛ̃. These whole first-person singular responses match those regional nominative continuations, preserving length, nasalization and source vowel notation. They are not assigned to aham merely from their nominative function; accusative molā and additional case endings are excluded.

proposals.evidence: The full tuvam article separates nominative, accusative, instrumental, genitive and dative developments; its addendum explicitly supplies Assamese tui. Hajong toi/tui is the neighboring familiar singular nominative and matches this complete regional pronoun. The link retains Turner’s discussion of analogical reshaping within the nominative family and leaves regional transmission open.
